profile.summary: LncBench is a collection of 15 RNA task datasets released with the LncRFM long non-coding RNA language model, each a Parquet file with sequence, label and split columns and its own training entry point in the LncRFM repository; two sets are test only. It is useful to developers of RNA language models who want ready-split datasets; there is no paper in the saved sources and no leaderboard.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: How well an RNA sequence model, fine-tuned or with a trained head, predicts per-task labels on 15 datasets named lnc_binary, RNAErnie-lncRNA, iLoc-lncRNA D1 and D2, lncATLAS-Localization, lncATLAS-RCI, Disease, Expression, POSTAR3-UPF1, mRNA-DMS, mRNA-Structure, 5UTR-MRL, RiNALMo-Splice, RNAChallenge and lncRNA-Structure. The README describes only some labels: Expression has five ordered categories, splice labels carry a donor or acceptor site and a value, DMS labels are per-base values and structure labels are base-pair index lists. The saved sources do not otherwise describe what each task measures.

DMS labels are per-base values, and structure labels are base-pair index lists.
Splice labels contain `site` and `value`; the entry point uses the requested site.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Each of the 15 files carries its own train, validation and test assignment in a split column, which the loader preserves. RNAChallenge and lncRNA-Structure hold test data only and are used with a trained task head. The Zenodo record says CC BY 4.0 covers the authors' own contributions and upstream data keep their original terms. The saved sources do not say where each dataset comes from or how its split was drawn.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Each task has its own training script. The scripts select the best epoch on a validation metric (F1, micro-F1, ROC AUC, Pearson correlation or Pearson r squared, depending on the task) and then report final test metrics. No aggregate score across tasks and no leaderboard are described. The README lists comparison models (RNA-FM, structRFM, RNAErnie, SpliceBERT, UTR-LM, RiNALMo micro, LncRNA-BERT) without results.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: Create the conda environment and install LncRFM, download the pretrained weights and the LncBench files from Zenodo, then run a task's training script with --data_file pointing at its Parquet file. The README's example trains a frozen-encoder adapter on iLoc-lncRNA_D1.

run_guide.summary: Install LncRFM and train and evaluate a frozen-encoder adapter on one LncBench task.
prerequisites: Conda, Python 3.10, PyTorch with CUDA 11.8 and a matching CUDA toolkit to build the state-space kernels.
LncRFM pretrained weights from https://zenodo.org/records/24356997, extracted to checkpoints/lncrfm_pretrained/.
The LncBench Parquet files from https://zenodo.org/records/24345986, placed in LncBench/ (the README example path).

steps.title: Get the code
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/chuyhu/LncRFM
cd LncRFM
git checkout --detach 429d79fb99dfecc180cbe8e41a554af0bb3bdaf1
steps.explanation: The README gives no clone command; this clones the repository named in the record and pins the reviewed commit.

steps.title: Install
steps.shell:
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate lncrfm
pip install --no-build-isolation causal-conv1d==1.4.0 mamba-ssm==2.2.2
pip install -e .
steps.explanation: As in the README's Installation section.

steps.title: Train and evaluate on iLoc-lncRNA_D1
steps.shell:
python LncDowntask/finetune_iloclnc_reference.py \
  --model_backend lncrfm \
  --finetune_scheme adapter --freeze_encoder --no_eval_test_each_epoch \
  --from_pretrained checkpoints/lncrfm_pretrained \
  --data_file LncBench/iLoc-lncRNA_D1.parquet --output_dir outputs/iloc
steps.explanation: The README's downstream example. Other tasks use the entry point listed for them in the README's table.

outputs: The script prints the best validation micro-F1 and the final test metrics, and saves the best checkpoint under the output directory.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
Weight and data downloads have no commands in the README; they must be fetched from the Zenodo pages.

notes: LncBench is released with the LncRFM model; no benchmark paper was found. The Zenodo API record shows no version string (the record's attribute says v1). GitHub reports the repository licence as NOASSERTION, but its LICENSE file is MIT with an MIT third-party notice. Metric directions are 'higher' because each script keeps the epoch with the highest validation value. The outputs line for the run guide comes from the iLoc script's final print statement, which reports best_val_micro_f1 and final_test metrics. Structured data_licence is null because the Zenodo record applies CC BY 4.0 only to the authors' contributions and says upstream data keep their original terms, which are not listed.
